title: Foundations: Power Metal - The Complete Guide
summary: What Power Metal is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Power Metal songs: Power metal is metal at its most triumphant: double-kick drums, soaring clean vocals about dragons and glory, and guitar solos like fireworks. Unironic, melodic, and faster than everything.

History: Helloween's Keeper of the Seven Keys (1987–88) invented European power metal; Blind Guardian, Stratovarius, and DragonForce (Through the Fire and Flames, 2006 — the Guitar Hero anthem) spread it worldwide.

How the songs work: Power Metal favors the keys of E, D, C, G. Common forms include Fast verse, huge chorus, neoclassical solo; Fantasy narratives across the album. Players should master double-kick drumming at 180 bpm first, then soaring tenor vocals, no growling. Speed and melody; standard tuning mostly.

title: Through the Fire and Flames - Power Metal Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Through the Fire and Flames by DragonForce (2006).
body:
Through the Fire and Flames — DragonForce, 2006. The Guitar Hero III final boss.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of C):
Cm | G# | D# | A#

This study chart uses the 'Epic i–VI–III–VII' progression, the Power Metal workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: fast verse, huge chorus, neoclassical solo. Listen for neoclassical shred solos — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Power Metal pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let neoclassical shred solos. Speed and melody; standard tuning mostly. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
